description: Mount Kenya Regenerative Agroforestry Project is a reforestation and afforestation  initiative designed and funded by Dutch Green Business. The Project aims to increase tree cover in Kenya through two distinct strategies: 1) restoring degraded or deforested areas in Kenya Forest Service lands with native species, and 2) planting agroforestry crop trees on individual farms where smallholders wish to benefit from the income that perennial nuts and fruits can provide. In both cases, site-appropriate tree species will be contributing to regional wildlife habitat or corridors, improving water infiltration, controlling erosion, and sequestering carbon, among other ecosystem services. Prior to project implementation, thousands of hectares of Kenya Forest Service land have been degraded or deforested over time, without the financial resources to restore them. In some cases, reforestation efforts have been attempted, but without the dedication of enough funds to guarantee the survival of these trees when threats like livestock grazing must be constantly warded off through employed patrols. The Project aims to change this dynamic by bringing in external up-front investment made possible through the anticipated sale of Verified Carbon Units generated through project activities. Similar financial barriers are faced by individual farmers, many of whom rely on annual crops like cabbage or potato, and do not have the resources to invest in trees that they are interested in. Their farms are currently lacking in canopy cover, with perhaps a few trees on the property boundaries that are cyclically harvested for fuelwood or timber.
